question: Does human-rated difficulty predict assisted one-move puzzle accuracy, and which board characteristics explain additional variation?
revision_disclosure: I narrowed the outcome after earlier local and hosted exploratory studies. I freeze this version before new responses; it is not a claim that this was my original unmodified design.
sample: 1000 fresh unique solver positions; low/middle/high rating allocation 334/333/333. Same 800 train and 200 held-out puzzles for both models. First 100 are a rating-balanced training pilot; never resample based on outcomes.
assistance: FEN, piece list, alphabetical complete legal UCI choices. No ratings, theme labels, game-phase labels, correct moves, engine evaluations or tools are provided.
scoring: Assisted one-solver-move puzzle accuracy: exact official solver move. I supply FEN, piece list and all unranked legal moves. Invalid/blocked/truncated answers count as failures; infrastructure failures remain pending.

scales.material_balance: solver material minus opponent material; P=1,N=B=3,R=5,Q=9

features.theme_rule: Separate binary indicators for candidate tags with at least 30 occurrences and 30 absences in the frozen 800 training puzzles; no outcome-based selection. Raw tags retained. Rare themes remain descriptive.
features.phase_rule: Use opening/middlegame/endgame tags. Exactly one tag => that phase; zero or multiple => unknown. Keep training-common phases (>=30 training puzzles); map the remainder to other. Baseline is the most frequent mapped training phase. Freeze dummy columns before responses.
features.solution_length: Verified as one; excluded as a constant. Side to move recorded descriptively, not added to this fixed regression.
features.sample_limitation: The frozen sample has 979/1000 mateIn1-tagged puzzles; generalization beyond mating tactics is limited. Raw tags are descriptive; only training-common prespecified indicators enter the final regression.

primary_regression: Pooled unpenalized binomial GLM: success ~ intercept + core board predictors + frozen theme indicators + game-phase indicators + Gemini identity indicator. All 1000 completed answers per model required. Puzzle-clustered standard errors; same puzzle is the cluster. Report odds ratios, ordinary 95% intervals and the prespecified two-sided rating coefficient test. Associations, not causal effects.
regression_gate: At least 50 successes and 50 failures in each model; full column rank; converged finite estimates and covariance; no perfect separation warning. If unsupported, report the reason without silently dropping predictors or changing the specification.
early_regression: After both models finish all 100 pilot training puzzles, fit an exploratory pooled regression using core board predictors and model identity only, puzzle-clustered SE. Require at least 15 successes and 15 failures per model. No primary significance claims or predictor tuning. The full theme/phase regression waits for the final sample.
tree: Separate sklearn CART per model, Gini, max_depth=3, min_samples_leaf=40, random_state=401, probability threshold .5. Predictors are the frozen full board features; no model identity within a per-model tree. Train on 800 only; no tuning.
early_tree: Descriptive CART per model on the same 100 pilot training cases, core board features, max_depth=2,min_samples_leaf=15,random_state=401; require >=15 successes and failures. Not a held-out performance claim.
heldout: After complete audited collection, freeze the tree before evaluating once on 200 held-out cases per model. Report accuracy/Wilson95, balanced accuracy, ROC AUC, Brier score, confusion matrix and training-majority baseline. Shared puzzle split prevents leakage. Primary association regression uses all responses; held-out claims apply only to the predictive tree.
pilot_policy: 8 capability checks then 20 training operational cases with zero-call replay proof, then extend to 100 training research cases per model. These 100 count toward final 1000 if request/scoring stays unchanged. Never replace completed wrong answers. Accuracy does not decide whether to keep a puzzle or tune a prompt.
versioning: New prompts, scoring or outcome-based predictor changes require a new version. Early snapshot is frozen once; collection cannot overwrite its inputs.
quota: Retain historical model usage for local guards; do not treat local budget stops as confirmed provider rate-limit errors. Setup mode makes no network requests.
